To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The proposed context management and reasoning framework is a novel approach to the development of UbiComp applications, which is based on the concept of hierarchical context modelling and reasoning; 2) The proposed context modelling framework is based on an ontology-based approach to context modelling, management, and reasoning; and 3) The proposed framework is based on the notion of context-awareness as a first-class concept, i.e., it provides mechanisms and methods to compose context-aware applications.
the use of ontologies is an effective way to model and manage context and that the use of ontology reasoning can be used for reasoning on context.
the ontology-based context management process can be used for building UbiComp applications that are able to adapt to changes in the environment and that are able to compose themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a generic context management framework for UbiComp systems that will provide the necessary support to the development of context-aware applications.
the design of an ontology-driven framework that enables the creation of a universal context model for AmI applications, and provides a mechanism for reasoning on the context information.
the following questions: How can we represent context information in a uniform and unambiguous way?

the proposed approach has the potential of becoming a standard for context modelling and management in UbiComp applications.
the approach presented is a good starting point for the development of a context-aware system.
the presented approach is able to provide an ontology-based context management, reasoning and composition process for UbiComps applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a new approach that is based on the use of ontologies for modelling and reasoning on context, which can be used to compose UbiComp applications.

we are developing an approach for the design of a context-aware UibComp system that is able to dynamically adapt to the environment changes, and to support the development of context-aware applications by providing an abstract model of the context and a context reasoning process.
we have developed an ontology-based context management process, which is able to manage and reason about context information, and a set of ontologies that can be used to compose UbiComp applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
context modelling can be done in an ontology-based manner, and that context reasoning is a key component of context-aware applications.

the proposed approach can be applied for the development of context-aware Ubi-Comp systems that can dynamically adapt to changes of users' activities, and at the meantime, can be composed from AmI arte- facts.
